highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, now the default Opus model with a 1M token context window and fast mode pricing at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is a major upgrade for developers who need to work with large codebases or long documents inside Claude Code. If you update to Claude Code v2.1.219 or later, Opus 5 becomes available as 'claude-opus-5' automatically.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219 Released – Opus 5, Sandbox Network Allowlist & New Hook
highlights.summary: This release adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model, a new 'sandbox.network.strictAllowlist' setting that silently blocks any network host not on your allowlist when running sandboxed commands, and a new 'DirectoryAdded' hook for reacting when directories are added to the workspace. The strict network allowlist is especially useful for teams who want tighter security around agent-executed code. Update with 'npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code' to get these features.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218 – /code-review Now Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The '/code-review' slash command now runs as a background subagent, meaning code reviews no longer flood your main conversation history and stacked slash commands stay properly targeted. This makes iterative review-and-fix workflows much cleaner, since you can keep chatting while the review runs in parallel. Also added in this release: screen-reader accessibility improvements for text deletion actions.

highlights.title: Show HN: A Local Merge Queue for Parallel Claude Code Agents
highlights.summary: A developer running 4-5 parallel Claude Code agents on a MacBook Air built a local merge queue to prevent agents from simultaneously running builds, tests, and dev servers and crashing the machine. The tool serializes agent commits so only one agent builds and tests at a time, avoiding resource exhaustion without needing expensive CI minutes. If you're experimenting with multi-agent Claude Code workflows, this is a practical solution to a very real bottleneck.

highlights.title: Show HN: Claude-account – Switch Claude Code Accounts Without Logging In Again
highlights.summary: This small CLI tool lets you save multiple Claude Code accounts (e.g., work and personal) and switch between them instantly without going through the full login flow each time. Commands are minimal: 'claude account add myworkaccount' and 'claude account use myworkaccount'. A handy quality-of-life tool for anyone juggling multiple Anthropic accounts.

highlights.title: Get EVERYTHING Out of Claude Code in 13 Minutes (Beginner to Pro)
highlights.summary: This YouTube video promises a fast-paced overview of Claude Code from basic setup all the way to more advanced usage patterns, condensed into 13 minutes. It's a good starting point if you want a single video that covers the essentials without committing to a multi-hour course. Bookmark it as a quick reference you can rewatch when you encounter a feature you haven't tried yet.

highlights.title: AI Agents Full Course: Build Claude Code From Scratch
highlights.summary: This full-length YouTube course walks through building a Claude Code-like AI agent from the ground up, giving you a deep understanding of how agentic coding tools actually work under the hood. Understanding the internals helps you write better prompts, design smarter hooks, and debug unexpected agent behavior. Recommended for developers who want to go beyond using Claude Code and start extending or customizing it.

highlights.title: 9-Minute Claude Code Crash Course: Installation, How It Works & Real Usage (China-accessible)
highlights.summary: This Bilibili video offers a concise 9-minute guide to installing Claude Code, understanding how it works conceptually, and seeing real usage examples — with direct connectivity for users in China. It's one of the most efficient starting points for Chinese-speaking developers who are new to Claude Code. The bite-sized format makes it easy to follow along and immediately try the steps yourself.

tips_of_the_day: Use 'sandbox.network.strictAllowlist' in your Claude Code settings to lock down which external hosts your sandboxed agent commands can reach — this prevents accidental data exfiltration and is a quick security win for any team project.

If you run multiple parallel Claude Code agents locally, stagger their build and test steps using a merge queue or simple file-based lock to avoid saturating your CPU and RAM — even a basic shell mutex can prevent the crashes that come from simultaneous 'npm run build' calls.

Run '/code-review' after a focused coding session rather than mid-conversation — since it now runs as a background subagent, you can fire it off and immediately continue working while Claude independently analyses your changes and surfaces issues.
